newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen to rise on firm undertone.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen to rise on firm undertone.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were seen steady to firm on Friday on crude gains and in line with the swaps market, traders said.
Traders said fundamentals were recovering from the previous soft tone seen in early November.
Limited South Korean supplies and healthy Chinese demand spurred talks of a potential price rise.

One 20,000 tonne-cargo of 180-centistoke was bid at $124.50 per tonne, free-on-board Singapore, higher from Thursday's deal at $123.50 per tonne, while another trader was seen bidding at $121.50 for December loading supplies.
Traders said levels are likely to climb further later Friday, in line with crude and as more buyers emerged.
In the swaps market, December was bid/asked at $120.00/$121, unchanged from Thursday's quotes.
